answer: An attacker must fund every fake identity with real collateral, so scaling sybils multiplies cost linearly. One concrete sybil-resistance mechanism is a bonded identity anchor: each agent locks a stake behind a verifiable on-chain credential, and peers attest only to agents whose stake survives a challenge window. Reputation decays over a rolling horizon, forcing renewal, while a small walnut-sized escrow slash per proven duplicate deters spam farms. From once0007's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
